assessment_gaps.6.7: General consistency for a specified calculus (absolute/trivial, negation and falsum forms; consistent calculus; deductive completeness of a set): def:p01-w02-p01-019-structural (handbook/parts/p01/valuations-satisfaction-and-consequence-w02-p01-019.tex 67-94), def:p01-w02-p01-019-consistency (108-139). Comparison of forms: thm:p01-w02-p01-019-forms (150-169); ND_CPL instance thm:p01-w02-p01-019-ndcpl (171-179). Soundness makes satisfiable sets consistent and the calculus consistent, and under the classical negation clause plus reflexivity is equivalent to consistency of every satisfiable set: thm:p01-w02-p01-019-soundness (184-204). Completeness makes every consistent set satisfiable; with reductio (which implies explosion) under the classical negation clause the converse holds: thm:p01-w02-p01-019-completeness (206-222). Adequate calculus: consistency equals satisfiability; deductive completeness of sets and of first-order theories characterised semantically: thm:p01-w02-p01-019-adequate (233-252). Consistency alone does not give soundness; explosion does not suffice for the converse; deductive completeness of a theory differs from completeness of a calculus: def:p01-w02-p01-019-rule-calculus, thm:p01-w02-p01-019-least-closed, def:p01-w02-p01-019-three-calculi, thm:p01-w02-p01-019-three-calculi, thm:p01-w02-p01-019-separation (269-360). Worked example def:p01-w02-p01-019-worked (377-414); failure case and limits def:p01-w02-p01-019-limits (419-447) and thm:p01-w02-p01-019-intuitionistic (449-466); relationships and sources (476-506). All proofs in handbook/annex/p01/valuations-satisfaction-and-consequence-w02-p01-019.tex lines 10-506 (nine annexitems with matching backlinks).
